content: The history of medicine in Canada originates from the oral traditions of the First Nations people. However, with the arrival of English and French settlers, the medical system became heavily influenced by military surgeons and Western medical practices. In the 18th century, Dr. David Parker, practicing in the Maritimes, became the first physician in Canada to perform surgery using an anesthetic. Another significant milestone in Canadian medical history was achieved by William Fraser Tolmie in British Columbia, who performed one of the first modern surgical procedures, which involved the removal of a tumor. During the 19th century, the establishment of medical schools in Upper Canada began in the 1820s. Among these was the Montreal Medical Institution, which later evolved into the Faculty of Medicine at McGill University. In the mid-1870s, Sir William Osler revolutionized medical education in the Western world by introducing a hands-on approach to medical training. The College of Physicians and Surgeons of Upper Canada was founded in 1839 and became permanently incorporated in 1869. In 1834, William Kelly, a Royal Navy surgeon, introduced the concept of disease prevention through sanitation measures, particularly in response to cholera epidemics. The 19th century also saw significant advancements in gender equality within the medical profession. Female physicians Emily Howard Stowe and Jennie Kidd Trout successfully campaigned for women to be admitted to medical schools and granted licenses by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario in 1871. In 1883, Emily Stowe spearheaded the establishment of the Ontario Medical College for Women, which was affiliated with the University of Toronto. In 1892, Dr. William Osler authored the seminal medical textbook The Principles and Practice of Medicine, which became the cornerstone of medical education in the Western world for the next four decades. In 1934, Dr. Wilder Penfield, a pioneering neurosurgeon, developed a groundbreaking surgical treatment for epilepsy known as the Montreal procedure. He also founded the Montreal Neurological Institute, which became a leading center for neurological research and treatment.
